key_insight: Rigid fibers in a Burgers-like microfluidic vortex show simple orientation dynamics: they precess with the vortex and align with it through strain, well captured by Jeffery equations plus the Burgers-vortex model.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact predictive framework for how elongated particles orient in vortex-dominated flows, useful for designing microfluidic, fiber-processing, and turbulence-relevant systems.
method: Microfluidic experiments on rigid, neutrally buoyant fibers in a streamwise stationary vortex
Theory using Jeffery orientation equations coupled to a Burgers-vortex flow model
Numerical simulations to compare particle motion with measured trajectories
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the measured orientation dynamics are accurately described by the coupled Jeffery–Burgers model, with only weak size- and inertia-induced deviations in the translational motion.
watch_item: The model is validated for a controlled moderate-Reynolds-number vortex, so performance in fully turbulent or strongly heterogeneous flows may require additional corrections.
paper_title: Orientation Dynamics of Rigid Fibers in a Microfluidic Burgers-like Vortex
